entries.answer: You’re welcome! Ask anything else about her work, or reach her directly at prishita.matreja@gmail.com.

Prishita Matreja is a CSE (Data Science) student at Bhagwan Parshuram Institute of Technology (2023–2027) and a paid AI Developer Intern at FTS Solutions. She builds LLM-powered tools with RAG, Ollama and FastAPI, writes Spring Boot backends, and has ensemble machine learning and Tableau work to her name.
The best way to reach Prishita is email: prishita.matreja@gmail.com. Her code is on GitHub at github.com/PrishitaM, and her deployed CleanSight app is at cleansight.streamlit.app.

Prishita is pursuing a B.Tech in CSE (Data Science) at Bhagwan Parshuram Institute of Technology, I.P. University (2023–2027), with a cumulative 88.6%. Before that, at Delhi Public School Dwarka, she scored 92.4% in Class XII and 95% in Class X.

Languages: Python, Java, C#, SQL, C++, JavaScript. AI: LLMs, LangChain, RAG, OpenAI API, Groq API, Ollama. ML: Scikit-learn, Random Forest, bagging and boosting ensembles, XGBoost, TensorFlow/Keras, PyTorch. Backend: FastAPI, .NET, Spring Boot, JWT. Data: MySQL, SQL Server, Supabase, Tableau, Streamlit.

entries.answer: Prishita uses LangChain to build retrieval pipelines: loading documents, chunking them, retrieving the relevant passages and passing them to an LLM. Her PDF RAG chatbot is built this way on top of local Ollama models.

At FTS Solutions she uses Ollama for log explanation, question answering and automated emails, and she designs prompts and retrieval so answers stay grounded in real data.

entries.answer: CleanSight is a deployed data profiling and cleaning web app built with Python, Streamlit, Pandas and Seaborn. It handles large datasets with interactive dashboards and outlier detection, and a research paper on it has been published. Try it at cleansight.streamlit.app.

Revenue Risk Radar analyses payment events to find failures and churn risk. It receives Razorpay Test Mode webhooks, classifies events like payment.captured and payment.failed, and uses the Groq LLM API with a RAG knowledge base to recommend recovery actions. A dashboard shows urgency and next steps, and automated support workflows escalate complex cases. Data lives in Supabase and SQL Server.
followups: Which LLM tools does she use?

entries.answer: The PDF RAG chatbot answers questions about uploaded PDFs. A LangChain pipeline splits documents into chunks and retrieves the most relevant passages, and a local Ollama model writes answers grounded in them, so documents stay on the machine. Data is stored in SQL Server (SSMS), and the code is on GitHub.
followups: Which LLM tools does she use?

entries.answer: The Car Insurance Claims Analysis is a Tableau storyboard for senior management. It has five dashboards, at least eight chart types and KPIs, two calculated fields and two parameters, plus an executive-summary dashboard with conclusions and recommendations. It covers customer profiles, claims, vehicle risk, segmentation and pricing.

The cab booking backend is a layered Spring Boot service with REST APIs for bookings, user management and fare calculation. It uses JPA with MySQL, Spring Security with stateless JWT authentication, Lombok, and distance-based fares with Google Maps integration. All endpoints were tested in Postman, and the code is on GitHub.

The AI Log Interpreter, built at FTS Solutions in C# and .NET, parses application logs, identifies errors and writes summaries with likely root causes. It uses Ollama for local LLM inference and RAG for context, with SQL Server behind it.
followups: What did she build at FTS Solutions?

entries.answer: The Ask AI web application at FTS Solutions is a React and FastAPI app that she enhanced with Ollama-powered answers, RAG-based knowledge retrieval, and automated email generation with escalation workflows for hard questions.

entries.answer: The file transfer service is a Windows Worker Service that checks for new files every 10 minutes and sends them to an SFTP server. If the internet is down, it keeps a local backup and sends the files when the connection returns.
followups: What did she build at FTS Solutions?

entries.answer: Her flagship ML project predicts visa approval (Certified or Denied). She benchmarked a Decision Tree baseline against Random Forest, Bagging, AdaBoost, Gradient Boosting and XGBoost on original, SMOTE-oversampled and undersampled data, tuned them with RandomizedSearchCV, and judged them on precision, recall and F1. Ensembles beat single models, and the analysis showed wages, experience and full-time roles drive approvals.

Prishita received an Outstanding Performance Certificate from IntersElite for the best project in her batch, completed the BCG X Forage job simulation on data for decision makers (April 2026), and was selected in rounds of Statathon and hackathons.

This assistant answers common questions instantly from a curated knowledge base. For anything outside it, it retrieves the closest facts about Prishita and asks an LLM on Groq to write the reply, so answers stay grounded in her real work.
